observation_summary: The date parsing logic in Joda-Time failed to correctly resolve dates when both week-based and month-based fields were provided in the format string, leading to incorrect year calculations.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves adding a second pass over the saved fields during the parsing process. This is a procedural change to the algorithm used to resolve date fields from the parser bucket, ensuring that dependencies between different field types (week-based vs. month-based) are correctly handled. It is not a simple guard (Checking) or a single value assignment (Assignment/Initialization), but a modification to the computational strategy of the parsing method.
evidence_used: The fix adds a loop that re-processes saved fields in DateTimeParserBucket.
The bug report indicates that mixing week-based and month-based fields caused incorrect parsing results.
The fix modifies the internal logic of the computeMillis method (implied by the context of the diff).

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix addresses the relationship between different date fields, the mechanism is a procedural change to the parsing algorithm (a second pass) rather than a structural association fix.
The fix is not just a guard or a validation check; it is an additional computational step (a second loop) to resolve the date correctly.
